title: Hidden auction surcharges can turn marketplace visibility into seller cost and a possible consumer-price channel
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission and 22 state attorneys general complaint against Amazon; institutional enforcement allegation, not a representative seller or consumer sample
geography: United States online search advertising auctions on Amazon.com and its mobile application

observations.period: August 31, 2026 FTC/state complaint; official release checked September 17, 2026

alleged_small_business_scope.value: more than 500,000 small- and medium-sized businesses

alleged_revenue_extraction.unit: alleged revenue from undisclosed advertising surcharges

alleged_consumer_pass_through.value: higher advertising costs were largely passed on to American consumers
alleged_consumer_pass_through.unit: FTC allegation; no seller-to-receipt estimate supplied

alleged_auction_change.value: Amazon represented second-price auctions but allegedly charged Sponsored Products advertisers their own winning bid close to 80% of the time by 2024

historical_alleged_frequency.value: approximately 30%-40% in 2021, 70% in 2022, and approximately 80% in 2024
historical_alleged_frequency.unit: Sponsored Products advertisers allegedly paying their own bid

case_status.value: complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington; legal result pending

observations.method: Official FTC release review; advertiser scope, auction rule, alleged surcharge, and consumer pass-through are retained as allegations and not converted into observed seller prices or household inflation.
observations.uncertainty: The release reports complaint allegations, not adjudicated conduct. It does not provide auction logs, seller margins, product-level price changes, customer purchases, quality, returns, or a denominator for consumers allegedly paying a pass-through.
observations.subgroup: Amazon advertisers, small and medium businesses, brands and sellers, shoppers exposed to sponsored placements, and consumers purchasing advertised products; advertiser and consumer units are not interchangeable.
observations.counterinterpretation: Sellers may absorb the charge, reduce bids, change quality or assortment, use another channel, or continue because visibility generates value; higher ad cost need not raise every price, and sponsored placement may improve matching for some customers.

related_sources.claim: Separate FTC and state Amazon marketplace case for the broader platform-control context; cases must not be pooled into one legal finding.
NBER field experiment supplies a separate short-run customer-choice comparison when Amazon-owned brands are hidden.

boundary: This record adds a named marketplace-advertising allegation linking hidden auction pricing to seller cost, visibility, and a possible consumer-price channel. It does not establish illegal conduct, seller pass-through, consumer price change, small-business exit, product choice, or household harm. The next test is an identifier-bearing seller/product auction-to-receipt record with bids, charges, placement, price, margin, quality, purchase, return, and exit kept separate.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: FTC press-release HTML retrieved without retaining a repository copy
